subject: Private endpoint outbound controls — egress handover & firewall ownership
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@medmovr.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security.team@medmovr.com
Date: Sun, 5 Oct 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — initial questionnaire and ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, our security team needs a concise ask list and the minimal set of IPs/FQDNs that Redwood's private endpoint will call outbound from our VPC. We're trying to avoid a broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress rule and prefer an allowlist model, plus a fallback story for maintenance windows.

Attached is our standard questionnaire (medmovr_egress_questionnaire.pdf). High-level asks from our side: 
- canonical outbound IP ranges (primary + failover) and expected port list
- whether TLS SNI or mTLS is required for control-plane interactions
- recommendations for short-lived proxy vs NAT gateway for reduced blast radius
- what telemetry/evidence you can provide that outbound connections originate from those IPs (for audits)

Can you put together a one-page matrix and owner list (who on Redwood will be the firewall contact) by Wednesday? Our audit window opens next Friday.

Best,
Sam
Security Engineer, MedMovr

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@medmovr.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — initial questionnaire and ask

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a draft egress matrix (redwood_egress_matrix_v1.csv) and a short evidence bundle outline we'll deliver for audit. Summary below and next steps.

Quick answers:
- Primary outbound: 34.201.112.0/28 (shared control plane) — port 443 outbound only (TLS).
- Failover pool: 34.201.112.16/28 (region-specified standby) — port 443.
- For private deployments we support both TLS SNI (required) and optional mTLS for control-plane calls; for MedMovr we'll enable mTLS on the control channel per your policy.
- Optional deployment pattern: customer NAT + outbound proxy (recommended) OR Redwood-managed egress pool. If you want minimal ops on your side, we can assign a static egress pool we manage; otherwise we provide the full set of hostnames for proxy allowlisting.

Evidence we can provide for audit: signed connectivity logs for the onboarding window, TLS cert subject + fingerprint used by control-plane, and an exported syslog sample showing source IP -> destination mapping for 7 days. We'll bundle that into safelist_evidence_bundle.zip.

Owner/contacts: 
- Redwood firewall owner (network ops): Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com) — will be primary for IP changes and rotation.
- Oncall for emergency egress changes: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com).
- Security liaison (policy & attestation): Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com).

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) You confirm whether MedMovr prefers Redwood-managed static egress or customer NAT/proxy.
2) We supply final IP/CIDR + CA cert thumbprint and formal evidence bundle by EOD Wednesday (10/8).
3) If you require ephemeral IPs rotated weekly, we will provide a rotation schedule and a signed attestation for each rotation.

If that works, I'll mark INF-2197 with the deliverables and loop in infra.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_egress_matrix_v1.csv
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@medmovr.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security.team@medmovr.com
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — initial questionnaire and ask

Ben — this is great, thanks. MedMovr prefers to operate the NAT/proxy (we have strict egress monitoring), but we will allowlist a Redwood-managed egress pool for scheduled maintenance or DR. Two clarifying items: 

1) Can you confirm whether the primary CIDR (34.201.112.0/28) will persist for at least 90 days? Our change board won't accept weekly churn without evidence.
2) For the mTLS option — what client cert rotation cadence do you expect from Redwood side (if we enable mTLS to the control-plane)?

Also, please include the minimal FQDN list for telemetry endpoints — we will prefer FQDN-based allowlisting where possible to reduce IP churn pain.

We'll accept the evidence bundle as long as it includes a verified mapping (syslog sample) that shows source IPs and the Redwood cert thumbprint in the handshake logs.

Sam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@medmovr.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — initial questionnaire and ask

Hi Sam — Karthik from Network Ops here. Quick answers inline and then a proposed succinct handover doc (below) for your change board.

- CIDR persistence: We can guarantee the primary CIDR (34.201.112.0/28) will be stable for a 120-day window post-onboarding. Any long-term rotation will be communicated 30 days in advance and accompanied by an attestation bundle for your auditors.
- mTLS rotation: Redwood rotates control-plane client certs quarterly; for mTLS we can provide a sync endpoint and an automated cert thumbprint notification when rotations occur. If you require weekly or custom cadence, we can negotiate as part of a Dedicated contract.
- FQDN list (minimal): api.control.redwoodinference.com, telemetry.redwoodinference.com, auth.redwoodinference.com — recommend FQDN allowlist + outbound port 443.

Handover (one-paragraph to paste into change board):
Redwood Inference private endpoint outbound connections originate from the Redwood-managed egress pool 34.201.112.0/28 (primary) with a failover pool 34.201.112.16/28. Control-plane and telemetry use TLS on port 443; TLS SNI is required, and mTLS is available as an opt-in configuration (client cert rotation quarterly). Redwood will provide an audit evidence bundle (signed connectivity logs, TLS cert fingerprints, and sample syslog mapping) within the onboarding window. Redwood network ops (Karthik Iyer) is the firewall owner for egress changes; Marissa Cole is the emergency oncall.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: get customer confirmation whether Redwood-managed egress pool is allowed for DR (BY EOD).
- Sam: confirm change-board template acceptance and preferred evidence delivery method (SFTP or secure Drive).
- Karthik: prepare attestation and sample logs (due 10/08 EOD).

Thanks — we'll treat this as priority to meet your audit window.

Karthik Iyer
Network Operations, Redwood Inference
